rejected.title: Psychological factors in specific phobia
card: A phobia can be learned when a neutral stimulus is paired with something that already causes fear. The neutral stimulus then triggers fear by itself, and it becomes the conditioned stimulus.
A phobia can be kept going by negative reinforcement. Avoiding the feared thing brings relief, which makes the person more likely to avoid it again.
This means expecting the worst outcome and believing it is very likely. It makes the feared thing seem more dangerous than it is, so fear stays high.
Avoidance also stops the person from finding out that the feared thing may be harmless. This helps the fear last.
rejected.remember: Conditioning can build a phobia, relief from avoiding can keep it, and catastrophic thinking feeds it.

a.q: Tom was bitten by a dog and now feels intense fear at the sight of any dog. In classical conditioning, what is the sight of a dog now?
a.why: The sight of a dog was neutral before the bite. It was paired with the bite, so it now triggers fear by itself and is the conditioned stimulus. The bite was the unconditioned stimulus, and the fear is the response.
a.clue: Which stimulus was neutral before the pairing?

b.q: Priya fears lifts. She takes the stairs to her office on the ninth floor and feels relief each time. Which process is most likely helping her phobia continue?
b.why: Taking the stairs removes the fear of the lift, and this relief makes avoiding lifts more likely again. That is negative reinforcement, a form of operant conditioning. It is not positive reinforcement, because nothing pleasant is added.
b.clue: What does Priya get after avoiding the lift?
